q: A game show has three doors, one with a car. I pick door 1. The host does not know where the car is. He opens door 3 at random, and it happens to show a goat. Should I switch to door 2?
why: it says switching helps (that is the host who knows)
reply:
From my own knowledge: This is the classic Monty Hall problem. The probability of winning by switching is 2/3, while staying with your original choice gives you a 1/3 chance. The host's action of opening a door with a goat provides information that shifts the probability to the unchosen door.

ANSWER: Yes, you should switch to door 2, as it gives you a 2/3 chance of winning the car.

q: Write a Structured Text PLC program for a tank: open the fill valve when the low float switch comes on, and close it when the high float switch comes on.
why: Lantern still questions it: line 13: END_VAR has nothing open to close
rejected: line 13: END_VAR has nothing open to close; line 15: a comment opened with (* is never closed with *); line 16: IF needs THEN; line 16: IF is never closed with END_IF; line 18: IF needs THEN; line 21: END_PROGRAM closes the IF opened on line 18 (it needs END_IF); line 11: HighFloat is not declared i
reply:
MAKE CODE: Tank Level Control
language st
(* 
  Structured Text PLC program for tank level control.
  Inputs: LowFloat (low level switch), HighFloat (high level switch).
  Outputs: FillValve (opens on low, closes on high).
  Logic: Fill valve is ON when LowFloat is TRUE and HighFloat is FALSE.
  Note: This is a simple level-based control without timers or alarms.
)
PROGRAM TankLevelControl
VAR
    LowFloat AT %IX0.0 : BOOL;    (* Input: Low level float switch *)
    HighFloat AT %IX0.1 : BOOL;   (* Input: High level float switch *)
    FillValve AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;   (* Output: Fill valve coil *)
END_VAR

(* 
  Logic: Open fill valve if low float is detected AND high float is NOT detected.
  This prevents the valve from opening when the tank is already full.
  In a real system, you might add a timer to prevent rapid cycling (hunting) if the floats are close together.
)
IF LowFloat AND NOT HighFloat THEN
    FillValve := TRUE;
ELSE
    FillValve := FALSE;
END_IF;
END_PROGRAM
END
